newsitem.title: USA: NY residents escape serious injury in blast.
newsitem.headline: NY residents escape serious injury in blast.

text.p: Residents of a quiet New York neighbourhood escaped serious injury early Tuesday when an explosion destroyed a Korean Presbyterian church and severely damaged three houses, officials said.
The New York City Fire Department said the blaze, which broke out shortly before 5 a.m. EDT in Flushing, Queens, might have been caused by a natural gas explosion and authorities were investigating.

"We suspect that it was a gas explosion but we haven't confirmed that," Fire Commissioner Thomas Van Essen said. "We do know that there was an unbelievable explosion that caused tremendous damage not only to the church but three houses."

Nine people were injured in the fire, which raged for more than two hours before it was extinguished by 250 firefighters. None of the injuries were serious or life-threatening, fire department spokesman Lt. Jerry Sanford said.
Power lines and trees were also knocked down.
